why: What each subagent may do. Read by .claude/hooks/agent_guard.py (PreToolUse); the main session (the orchestrator) never goes through here: settings.json and the user's OK govern it. Terminal rules look at what a command DOES (the program that runs and its arguments), not at its words: a commit message or a `git add` that NAMES a protected script passes; running it doesn't. Every rule has a unique id: scripts/verify/guard_selftest.py checks that removing any of them changes some case (otherwise the rule has no test). The guard that applies is the main branch's: a change made on a branch only takes effect once merged. CUSTOMIZE PER PROJECT: `protected`, the infra/dependency rules and the main branch name in `git-main`.
protected_why: Regex of the scripts that change SHARED state (a database, infra, deploys): only the orchestrator runs them, with the user's OK. Every rule that says {protected} uses it, so it lives in one place. Example name; replace it with yours (e.g. `db_apply\.py|deploy\.sh`).

accepted_risks.why: The guard stops mistakes by cooperative agents, not an attacker. These evasions are known and not pursued: closing them would cost fragile rules or block normal work. If one starts happening by mistake, close it with its case in the self-test.

list.risk: A task runner (make, npm run, just, a shell script) whose recipe does something forbidden
list.why: The guard judges the command line, not what scripts do inside. Keep protected actions out of task runners, or add an `executes` rule for that target.

list.risk: awk with system() or getline from a command
list.why: awk is used daily to read; analyzing its program is a whole other interpreter.

list.risk: Reviewer writes from inline code (node -e fs.writeFileSync, python -c open(...,'w')) or dd
list.why: Scanning all inline code for writes would give constant false positives; the reviewer writes with redirections, cp or sed, which are checked.

list.risk: Formatters that write by default (black, ruff format, gofmt -w) run by the reviewer
list.why: Its instructions say not to; one rule per formatter would be fragile. --fix and --write are blocked.

list.risk: gh api to merge or close a PR (instead of gh pr merge)
list.why: An agent that merges by mistake uses gh pr merge, which is blocked.

list.risk: Copying a protected script in two steps (to a temp folder, then mv/cp elsewhere)
list.why: Each step alone is normal; following content across commands would need state. A mistake doesn't chain that.

list.risk: Symlinking binaries to /tmp and running them under another name
list.why: It takes intent; a mistake doesn't produce it.

list.risk: grep -r for secrets without naming the .env (grep -r API_KEY .)
list.why: The guard blocks naming the .env; a recursive grep can pass through it. settings.json also denies Read of .env.

list.risk: zsh =(…) (process substitution to a temp file)
list.why: zsh isn't the agents' shell; bash's <(…) is covered.
